chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Miserliness contains all other evil vices, and it is the rein with which one is led to every evil.

key_terms.زِمَامٌ: Rein (of a horse), used metaphorically for control
key_terms.مَسَاوِئِ الْعُيُوبِ: Evil vices or bad character traits

ai.seo_question: What is the root of all moral vices according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies miserliness not merely as a financial trait but as the comprehensive source of all moral deficiencies, effectively acting as a 'rein' that guides the soul toward every form of evil. This concept is deeply rooted in Shia ethical tradition, where al-bukhl is often contrasted with generosity (al-jud) as the primary indicator of spiritual health and divine proximity. The metaphor highlights the controlling nature of this vice, suggesting that once the heart is bound by stinginess, it loses its capacity for other virtues.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 378. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Miserliness contains all other evil vices and is the rein with which one can be led to every evil.
